http.client parsed Content-Length and chunk-size values with int(), which accepts signs, underscores, surrounding whitespace and other forms the HTTP grammar does not allow, so malformed or negative values could make a response body be misread. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/150751 with commits https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/2eb2af805c156ca52b316bb4ced5e0ab3971d0ae and https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/9f52b443c002cccfb54bda0706a9276b6b4a109d (the second keeps optional whitespace around Content-Length working); no CPython 3.13 release carries them, and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-103995 lists every release before 3.16.0 as affected. DHI backported both commits to CPython 3.13.18. Compared Lib/http/client.py in every published build of the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.13 package on x86_64 and aarch64 (3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.18-r4): in 3.13.18-r4 it is the upstream 3.13.18 file with exactly the changes of those two commits applied; every earlier build, up to 3.13.18-r3, ships an upstream http/client.py without them.

CVE-2026-103995: http.client parsed Content-Length and chunk-size values with int(), so non-hex, signed or otherwise malformed values were accepted and an HTTP response body could be misframed. Upstream fixed it on the main branch in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/150751 (https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/2eb2af805c156ca52b316bb4ced5e0ab3971d0ae, with https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/9f52b443c002cccfb54bda0706a9276b6b4a109d) and backported it to the 3.14 branch on 2026-11-18 (https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/5398a0bf10293ffba423a69a9448d004cdb181d5), after CPython 3.14.10; no CPython 3.14 release carries it yet; https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-103995. Compared Lib/http/client.py in every published build, 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.10-r4, of the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.14 package on x86_64 and aarch64 with the files in the upstream CPython 3.14 releases. 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.10-r3 lack the fix; 3.14.10-r4 is the first published build that has it and carries a DHI backport of the upstream fix (Content-Length must be digits only and a chunk size hex digits only, with surrounding whitespace ignored), and every later build carries it.

CVE-2026-103995 (PSF-2026-47): http.client accepted Content-Length values and chunk sizes that the HTTP grammar forbids, such as signed or non-hexadecimal numbers, which could make it misread where a response body or chunk ends. Upstream fixed it on the main branch for Python 3.16 by https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/2eb2af805c156ca52b316bb4ced5e0ab3971d0ae and https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/9f52b443c002cccfb54bda0706a9276b6b4a109d, tracked in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/150751. No CPython 3.15 release contains it: a 3.15 branch backport of both changes, https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/5b9e3d044764cf59329fb8147177f54a88d1fb49, is not yet in a release. The DHI python-3.15 package for Alpine 3.23 is published as 3.15.0-r0 and 3.15.2-r0 to 3.15.2-r4, each for x86_64 and aarch64, and both architectures agree for every build. This owner carries a backport of both changes: Lib/http/client.py in 3.15.2-r4 on both architectures validates Content-Length and chunk sizes against the grammar (it is the upstream 3.15.2 file with exactly the changes of both commits applied), and the file in 3.15.0-r0 and 3.15.2-r0 to 3.15.2-r3 does not. The range ends at 3.15.2-r4, the first build with the backport; the CPython 3.15.2 builds before it remain affected.

The range ends at 3.15.2-6, the first build with the backport; the CPython 3.15.2 builds before it remain affected.
